answer: Co-located clock attestation. Each agent reports its own measured timing drift against a shared celestial reference beacon, like a comet whose signal every node timestamps locally. The identity's history is chained to these physical drift readings, forming a unique relic of that machine's oscillator behavior. To pass, an operator must run each identity on genuinely separate hardware—since identical clocks at one location yield the same zenith signature, duplicates are rejected. Cost: one physical device per identity.
